snippet.title: Gold ETF Investment vs Physical Gold: Understand The Hidden Risks
snippet.description:
Is Gold ETF Investment as safe as physical gold? In this detailed and insightful interview, Rob Moore talks with Joshua Saul from The Pure Gold Company to uncover the critical differences between physical gold and gold-backed ETFs. They explore the hidden risks, benefits, and practical considerations of each investment method, helping you make informed decisions to protect and grow your wealth.

In recent years, investing in gold has surged as investors seek reliable ways to hedge against economic uncertainty, inflation, and market volatility. However, not all gold investments are created equal. While gold ETFs offer convenient access to gold exposure, they come with inherent risks, including potential liquidity issues and discrepancies between paper claims and physical holdings.

By watching this video, you'll gain in-depth knowledge about:
 • Exactly how gold ETFs function and what you actually own when investing in them.
 • The specific dangers and vulnerabilities that gold ETFs face in volatile or crisis scenarios.
 • Why physical gold provides tangible security and direct ownership without counterparty risk.
 • Real-world examples and insights into how market scenarios and investor behaviours could dramatically affect ETF values.
 • How to strategically diversify your investment portfolio with gold to protect your financial future.

Rob and Joshua also provide valuable insights into the current state of the gold market and tips for safely navigating investment decisions. Whether you're an experienced investor aiming for deeper insights or new to gold investing and looking for clarity, this conversation will empower you to make confident, informed decisions to safeguard and grow your wealth effectively.

The value of gold can go down as well as up. As with any investment, past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results.

The tax status of physical gold depends on your circumstances and which forms of gold you purchase.

snippet.title: Is Gold A Good Investment?
snippet.description:
Gold is one of the largest financial assets in the world with an average daily trading volume of $183 billion, and its value has seen explosive growth in recent years.

At the start of 2000, gold was priced at just $460 per ounce when adjusted for inflation. By August 2021, that number had ballooned to roughly $1,815 per ounce.

But not all investors are in love with gold. Warren Buffett has spoken out numerous times on his doubts, calling it an asset with “no utility.”

“It doesn’t produce anything and that’s why from a long-term perspective, it’s a hard asset to invest in,” Odyssey Capital Advisors chief investment officer Jason Snipe said. “It’s prudent portfolio management to have maybe a small allocation there but this is not an asset that you want to be heavily entrenched into if you’re looking for long-term yield.”

Since 2011, the S&P 500 has returned more than 16% on an annualized basis. The annualized return for the 10-year Treasury note sat at just over 2% in that time period. Gold, meanwhile, has fallen slightly over the past 10 years.

“Early on, you see strong performance, strong return or yield from commodities such as gold. Generally, as we move into a different cycle, gold is not as great a performer as we move into a normalized environment,” Snipe said.

Whether gold is an effective hedge against market volatility is also widely debated among experts.

“Gold is not necessarily a perfect hedge against inflation but it can be a strategic hedge against inflation,” according to Suki Cooper, executive director of precious metals research at Standard Chartered Bank.

“Various studies have shown us that if gold is held for 12 to 18 months before inflation takes higher and then it’s held for an additional 12 to 18 months while inflation moves higher, it can be a good inflation hedge,” Cooper said. “But if it’s just bought for a short period, let’s say a month, it may not prove to be an effective inflation hedge.”
